Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

Two targeted, fully Figma-grounded fixes on Step 5 (ZimmProductCardContent) of the SFCC-236 build, found during the visual checkpoint. Both were previously either wrong or built on an unconfirmed assumption; both are now backed by direct Figma citations pulled this session — do not re-derive, just apply exactly as specified and verify.

## Files to modify (only these 2)
```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/zimmProductCardContent.css.ts
```
Do not touch `index.stories.tsx` or `index.test.tsx` unless a test assertion literally breaks because it checked the old (wrong) copy/token/alignment value — in that case update only the specific assertion, don't restructure the test file.

## Fix 1 — name/bag-icon row vertical alignment
File: `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`, the `nameRow` part.

Currently: `alignItems: 'flex-start'`.

Figma ground truth (pulled directly via `get_design_context` on node `40002163:41441`, the real assembled Desktop/Default/PLP-PDP card — not just the standalone documentation set): the "Card heading" (name) element resolves to a taller effective box than the "Icons"/`touchContainer` (bag icon) element, because of their different internal padding (name: 8px padding around 16px line-height ≈ 32px tall; icon: 4px padding around a 16px icon = 24px tall). With the row's `alignItems` set to `flex-start`, these two different-height children top-align, producing a visible ~4px vertical offset between the icon's optical centre and the name text's optical centre — this is exactly the visual misalignment that was spotted in the live Storybook render.

Change `nameRow`'s `alignItems` from `'flex-start'` to `'center'`. This vertically centers both children regardless of their differing internal padding, which is the correct, robust way to align a text label against an icon button of a different height in a horizontal flex row — and matches what the design visually shows (name and icon centred together), even though Figma's own auto-generated code approximation happens to specify `items-start` at the container level (Figma's codegen for auto-layout doesn't always perfectly capture visual centering achieved via matching padding in the original design tool).

Update the existing comment above `nameRow` (currently explaining the `gap` value) to also note why `alignItems: 'center'` is used, citing this reasoning briefly.

## Fix 2 — notify-me control: wrong copy, wrong colour token, wrong/placeholder spacing
This control had NO real Figma grounding when originally built — it was inferred from the Jira AC's prose ("a notify me link appears on hover"). It has since been found in the actual design: node `40002163:41468` (Desktop, Hover, PLP/PDP, Unavailable=True — the exact state the AC describes), which shows the real control clearly. Pulled directly via `get_design_context` on that node:

**Real copy:** the literal text is **"NOTIFY ME"** (all-caps, two words) — not "Notify me when back in stock". The extra phrase was invented; remove it entirely.

**Real component identity:** in Figma, this is not a bespoke button — it's an instance of the same generic `CTA/Link` atom used elsewhere in this component set (node `40001908:28374`/`40001908:28368`, 57×24), just with contextual text swapped to "NOTIFY ME" in this state. Its styling per the design-context pull:
- Text style: Figma names it `Default/Link-sm` (font-size `brand/font/size/300` ≈12px, weight 500/bold, line-height `brand/font/lineheight/350`, letter-spacing `brand/font/letterspacing/negative-100`) — this maps to this codebase's own `textStyle: 'linkSm'`, which is **already what the recipe currently uses** — do not change the `textStyle` value, it was already correct.
- **Colour: `alias/color/link/default`** (a real, distinct semantic token in Figma) — **NOT** `text/default`, even though both happen to resolve to the same hex (`#191919`) in this palette. The current recipe uses `color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)'`, which is the wrong semantic category — a real `--zimm-color-link-default` token already exists in this codebase (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:79`). Change the colour to `var(--zimm-color-link-default)`.
- Underline: the Figma text carries a genuine underline (`underline decoration-from-font`) — check whether the current `textStyle: 'linkSm'` already includes underline styling (it likely does, since it's a link text style) by reading `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s `linkSm` definition; if it doesn't already underline, that's a separate, larger finding to report rather than hack around here (do not add an ad-hoc `textDecoration` override to work around a textStyle that's supposed to already handle this — report it instead if you find a mismatch).

**Real spacing:** the design-context pull shows the "Content" wrapper (the flex column holding name-block, price, and this notify-me link when present) applies a **uniform 24px gap** (`var(--alias/space/600, 24px)`) between ALL of its direct children — including between price and this notify-me link. This is the exact same `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` token already used elsewhere in this same recipe for the name-block-to-price gap. The current recipe's `notifyMeButton.marginTop` uses `var(--zimm-scale-m)` (16px) with a comment saying it's "a placeholder — no Figma spec exists... pending UI-designer sign-off." That comment is now out of date — a real, confirmed value exists. Change `marginTop` to `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` and update/remove the "no spec exists, placeholder" comment to instead cite the real source (the same `Content` wrapper's uniform 24px gap, node `40002163:41470`, confirmed via `get_design_context`).

**In `index.tsx`:** change the `notifyMe` message's `defaultMessage` from `'Notify me when back in stock'` to `'Notify me'` — wait, check the EXACT casing Figma shows: the raw text node is `"NOTIFY ME"` in all-caps. Check how this codebase's other all-caps-looking UI text is actually authored — e.g. does `ZimmProductName`'s "Product Name" or the Tag's "LABEL" get authored as normal-case text with a CSS `text-transform: uppercase` applied by the textStyle (which is the pattern I'd expect, since raw copy should stay sentence-case/normal-case for i18n and accessibility reasons, with visual capitalisation handled purely by CSS) — read `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s `linkSm` definition to check if it already applies `textTransform: 'uppercase'` or similar. If `linkSm` already visually uppercases its text via CSS, author the `defaultMessage` as normal sentence case (`'Notify me'`) and let the textStyle handle the visual caps — do NOT hardcode literal `'NOTIFY ME'` as the translatable string (that would be wrong for i18n — a translator should translate "Notify me", not a pre-capitalised string). If `linkSm` does NOT already uppercase, report this as a finding rather than deciding unilaterally which layer should own the capitalisation.

## After both fixes, verify:
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
npm run test
```
All must be clean/green. Confirm via `git status --porcelain` that only `zimmProductCardContent/` files (and possibly the pre-existing unchanged `theme/components/index.ts` diff) show any change — nothing else. Do NOT stage or commit.

Report exactly what changed (before/after for each of the two fixes), what you found when checking `linkSm`'s definition for underline/uppercase handling (and what you did as a result), and confirm all verification commands pass.

13	 * `data-card-slot` values on this component's own DOM so that organism's own recipe can target
14	 * these descendants for hover-reveal styling without reaching into implementation details.

47	/**
48	 * `ZimmProductName`'s own heading-level prop, read off the atom's real signature via a utility
49	 * type rather than a hand-typed duplicate union (typescript.md: "prefer utility types over
50	 * hand-rolled duplicate shapes... a hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
51	 * original changes"). Its type param is `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` — note this is NOT `'h2' | 'h3' |

67	   */

71	   * `ZimmNavItem`/`ZimmContactIconRow`'s CMS-sourced hrefs, this is an SFCC-generated product URL,

104	   * `data-card-slot="sizeChips"` note.
105	   */

134	 *

136	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
137	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
138	 */

140	  name,
141	  headingLevel,
142	  href,
143	  currentPrice,
144	  originalPrice,
145	  isPriceLoading,
146	  showAttributes,
147	  colour,
148	  size,
149	  showBag,
150	  isUnavailable,
151	  onAddToBag,
152	  showSizeChips,

167	  // alone, so an organism that sets the flag without wiring a real callback silently renders
168	  // nothing rather than an inert button.
169	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
170	
171	  return (
172	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot="content">
173	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
174	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
175	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
176	        </ProductNameLink>
177	
178	        {showBag && (
179	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper}>
180	            <chakra.button
181	              type="button"
182	              __css={styles.bagButton}
183	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
184	              disabled={isUnavailable}
185	              onClick={() => {
186	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
187	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
188	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
189	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
190	                if (isUnavailable) return;

195	            </chakra.button>
196	          </chakra.div>
197	        )}
198	      </chakra.div>
199	
200	      {showAttributes && (

202	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colour}</chakra.span>
203	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
204	        </chakra.div>
205	      )}
206	
207	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot="price">
208	        <ZimmProductPrice
209	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
210	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
211	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
212	          isLive={false}
213	        />
214	      </chakra.div>

218	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup

220	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
221	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
222	          />
223	        </chakra.div>
224	      )}

226	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
227	        <chakra.button type="button" __css={styles.notifyMeButton} onClick={onNotifyMe}>
228	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
229	        </chakra.button>
230	      )}
231	    </chakra.div>
232	  );
233	};
